findings.part: engine core: firing hook placed inside _apply_result, versus the transition hooks in dispatch (risk 11 / harness_changes engine core)
findings.claim: Draft: "Knowledge, item commit and lint side effects key on history rows after the save and are unchanged [M, _item_commit and _knowledge_close]" (risk 11), so pausing inside _apply_result is side-effect neutral.
findings.evidence: [M] True for knowledge and item commit, false for lint. lint.on_transition returns early when after.get('status') != 'active' (skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_lint.py, on_transition: `if mode not in ("fix","report") or after.get("status") != "active": return writes, None`). dispatch computes _lint_transition(core, root, state, updated) on the already-paused state, so lint_view(after).status is 'paused'. Run: I patched a scratch copy of d1cca62f with the draft's design (stop_at key, _stop_check wrapping _apply_result, control pause, two revisions in one save) and drove the real CLI (scratchpad/stop-points-design/lens-engine/lensA_lint.py). Completing skill-validate with after:skill-validate armed paused at static-checks and wrote only lint/<action>-inventory.md; the unarmed run also wrote lint/<action>.md. After `resume`, the static-checks packet has no 'ShipLoop lint (supporting output ...)' block, and nothing reruns the pass (lint.render_lines only reads records and prints nothing when the record is absent, so the loss is silent). In fix mode the first-entry auto-fix (allow_fix=first) is skipped the same way. The same early return skips the verify report-lint for after:static-checks (read, not run: my static-checks complete was refused in both arms). lensD_entry_runs.py shows the other entry writes are not lost: test-loop contract (tests/<action>-contract.json) and lint item base (lint/items/W2.md) are identical armed and unarmed. So 2 of the 33 forms (after:skill-validate, after:static-checks) make a resumed run differ from an uninterrupted one, defeating the owner's 'test later stages without paying planning again'. The proposed tests cannot see it: the 33-stage grid (I2) is pure API and never calls dispatch or _lint_transition, and the CLI tests (I3, I4) stop only at intake, discovery and spec.
findings.correction: Run the transition hooks (_lint_transition) on the un-paused accepted state and pause afterwards. Either apply the stop in dispatch, in both the complete and improve-complete branches, after _lint_transition and before save (keep _stop_check pure and unit-tested; the cost is that pure apply, the dry run and SEED_SCRIPT no longer fire stops), or make lint_view treat a held stop as active. Then add a CLI-level test (pure_advance_to, arm after:skill-validate, real `complete`, `resume`) asserting the lint record exists for the static-checks action, and the same for after:static-checks. Correct risk 11: lint is keyed on status, not on history rows.

findings.part: held packet text, status block and SKILL.md (packet_text, harness_changes CLI verb row, owner decision 6)
findings.claim: Draft: the held packet embeds the script-rendered status block, status_block is left untouched, SKILL.md is NOT edited, and the packet tells the model to end its turn with no resume command.
findings.evidence: [M] status_block's paused/blocked branch prints 'Stopped: paused: <reason>. The packet prints the resume command.' for every paused state. I rendered it on a held state: 'Stopped:   paused: paused at the requested stop point after:skill-validate. The packet prints the resume command.' (461 chars). The draft's packet_text embeds '<status block, script rendered>', so the held packet says in the same breath 'Do not run resume' and 'The packet prints the resume command.' It also prints no such command. [M] SKILL.md 'Follow the current packet' step 5 tells the model: 'If a packet is paused or blocked, resolve its stated condition and use its printed `resume` command once.' SPEC S-3 says when a card and a script disagree the script wins and the disagreement is a defect to fix. Standing model-read guidance (resume once) therefore contradicts the one behaviour the design depends on, the model not self-resuming (risk 2, the only evidence being n=5 short probes whose earlier packet did print the resume command). Report 1 listed the status line as a prototype shortfall, but the draft's 'status_block untouched' decision reintroduces it. The ~700-character estimate is also understated: the status block alone is 461 characters (the total is unmeasured).
findings.correction: Add a held-state branch to status_block's paused line (e.g. 'Stopped: paused at a requested stop point; end the turn'). Active packets stay byte-identical because the branch is reachable only when held. Add one SKILL.md sentence making a packet that names a requested stop point an exception to 'use its printed resume command'; the model never resumes it. Add a test that the held packet contains neither the phrase 'prints the resume command' nor a resume invocation. Write the S-6 carve-out into S-16 itself: a held packet carries no recovery command by design, so S-6's 'the callback and the recovery command' needs an explicit, dated exception rather than only an owner-decision bullet.

findings.part: stop-at verb: set semantics (PLUMBING v1, resume section)
findings.claim: Draft: 'Identical --set is idempotent', 'A pending record may be replaced', and (resume section) 'To stop again, stop-at --set replaces the old record'.
findings.evidence: [I] The three statements conflict for a consumed record. The draft says the verb bumps the revision 'like set_lint_mode', and set_lint_mode is `if state.get('lint') == value: return deepcopy(dict(state))`. If set_stop_at copies that and compares only `when`, then re-arming the same spec after it fired (reached non-null) is a silent no-op that exits 0 and prints 'armed'. Grammar v1 has no #n, so 'stop after implement of each item' needs exactly that re-arm after every resume. The harness would believe it armed; the stop would never fire for the next item. The grading would not mark it passed (held is false at the end), but the run is wasted.
findings.correction: Specify idempotence as equality of the whole record, {when: X, reached: null}. A consumed record with the same `when` must be replaced by a fresh one with reached null. Add a test: arm after:implement, fire, resume, re-arm the same spec, fires again at the next item.

findings.claim: Draft: refuse arming 'a prelude or outer stage that already has a done row'; inner stages are never refused.
findings.evidence: [M] reconcile() in shiploop_navigator.py sets updated['stage'] = the target planning stage with a new action and keeps the earlier done rows in history (it adds a row with outcome 'reconcile'). After a reconcile, the cursor is back at spec and spec will be accepted again, yet 'has a done row' refuses after:spec as already accepted. The rule is also a second implementation of 'stage accepted' beside _accepted_done (S-12).
findings.correction: Refuse on the cursor (the stage is behind the current cursor, or the run is past it), not on 'has a done row'. Reuse _accepted_done or the stage order. Add a reconcile-rewind arming test.

findings.part: SPEC S-16 wording and S-11 ordering (spec field, risk 11)
findings.claim: S-16 text: the pause is saved 'after the transition's commits and before the next packet is issued', 'waits on no input', and 'a point that is already past is refused when it is armed'.
findings.evidence: [M] dispatch order for complete and improve-complete is apply (stop decided) then completion_guard, then _lint_transition, then save, then _lint_finish, then _item_commit, then _knowledge_close, then emit. The stop is saved before the item and knowledge commits, not after. _knowledge_close swallows a failure, printing 'the next accepted stage commits it' and returning, so after a stop at the last stage a failed knowledge commit (S-11) is not retried until the owner resumes. The harness's 'never kills the host before the stop is saved' is weaker than 'before the commits', so any reader keyed on state.md alone can see the repository before the commit lands. 'Waits on no input' contradicts 'the run continues in place when the owner resumes it': a held run waits for a resume, and a forgotten armed stop stalls an unattended run (the S-14 hazard the draft itself cites against the environment variable). 'Already past is refused' holds only for prelude and outer stages; inner stages are never refused (draft's own rule).
findings.correction: Reword S-16: 'saved in the same transition that accepts the stage; the item and knowledge commits then run before the packet is printed'. Say the run waits for the owner's resume and rests on S-14's rule that an owner-requested stop is opt-in, like --delegation. Say refusal applies to prelude and outer stages only. Have the harness treat 'reached' as complete only once the host has exited or the packet was printed, and state that a failed knowledge commit at a stop is retried at resume.

findings.part: release process: change notes per commit (increments I2, I8, I9)
findings.claim: Draft: I2 changes skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py in its own commit; the change note changes/shiploop/stop-point.md is added in I3.
findings.evidence: [M] scripts/check-release-boundary.py rejects, per ordinary commit, a change to skills/<leaf>/ without a note under changes/<leaf>/ or a final-paragraph 'No-Change-Note:' trailer ('it excuses only the commit that carries it'; changes/README.md). I2 (and I8, I9, which also edit skills/shiploop) list no note, so the I2 commit fails CI as drafted. I0 is docs-only and needs no skill note.
findings.correction: Move changes/shiploop/stop-point.md (bump: minor) into I2, or give I2, I8 and I9 a note or a No-Change-Note trailer with its reason.

findings.claim: Draft: the I2 grid, driven by the dry run's oracle rows, fails on unchanged code and covers the 33 stages; I3 and I4 exercise the real CLI.
findings.evidence: [M] I2 fails on unchanged code only because set_stop_at and the key do not exist (AttributeError and 'unexpected: stop_at'), which pins nothing about behaviour; the mutation checks that would are 'done once by hand'. The grid is pure API and bypasses dispatch, where the lint, item-commit, knowledge-close and contract hooks run (finding 1 shows a regression in exactly that layer). The CLI tests fire only at intake, discovery and spec. Verified correct: with the draft's wrapper, the real CLI and real Improve child fire at the improve-complete import and not at the producer complete; replaying the producer complete and the improve-complete leaves state.md unchanged (rc 0); `pause` on a held run is refused; `resume` returns the same action id and `complete` then parks the next stage's child without re-firing (lensB_resume.py). Five specs (after:step-plan, test-spec, baseline, test-author, test-red) on a docs-only item all pause at the same revision with the cursor on implement (lensC_na.py), as the draft's owner decision 5 expects.
findings.correction: Add a small CLI-level stop matrix (pure_advance_to, then the real `complete`, then `resume`) for the stages whose next stage has entry runs: select-work (lint-base), test-green and regression (test-loop contract), static-checks (inventory, quality contract, advisory lint) and verify (report-lint). Assert the entry artifacts equal an unarmed run. Keep the hand mutation checks, but encode at least the drop-current_stage and drop-row-scan mutants as tests.

findings.part: held predicate, --clear and the harness reader (S-12; state-key section; run.py grading)
findings.claim: Draft: held is derived in the engine (stop_held) and the harness reads stop_at back from state.md; the behaviour of --clear on a held run is unspecified.
findings.evidence: [M] run.py grade_shiploop parses state.md with store.read_record and does not import the installed navigator (SEED_SCRIPT is the only place that runs the plugin's own navigator in a separate interpreter). The held test (status paused and reached.revision equal to revision) would be implemented twice (S-12). [I] `stop-at --clear` on a held run would drop the record but leave status paused with a reason naming a stop that no longer exists; the packet then falls back to the generic paused packet, which is cut at PRINT_LIMIT 16,000 (confirmed: a paused replay in lensB printed the 'Full packet:' pointer) and loses its Resume line, re-exposing pre-existing defect 13.
findings.correction: Expose held through the engine (a held field in `status` or `hook-status` output), or call it from the harness the way SEED_SCRIPT does, so there is one definition. Refuse `--clear` while held (resume first), consistent with `--set`, and test it.
